title: Russian Iskander-Kh31-Drone Barrage Hits Five Oblasts, Knocks Out Power in Chernihiv Region
detail: Russian forces launched an overnight barrage of one Iskander-M ballistic missile, one Kh-31P anti-radar missile, and around 150 Shahed-type, Gerbera, and Parodiya drones into August 25. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted roughly 124 of the drones; the remainder struck 17 locations, damaging residential, logistics, agricultural, and railway infrastructure across Chernihiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Kyiv, Kharkiv, and Zaporizhzhia oblasts. A power facility was hit in Chernihiv district and the city of Slavutych, cutting electricity to more than 30,000 subscribers; grid operator Ukrenergo also reported outages in Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, Kherson, and Sumy oblasts. Energy crews said restoration work would begin once the security situation allowed.

title: Geran-3 Drones Hit Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia, 11 Injured
detail: In a separate wave on the evening of August 25 (reported ~20:50), Russian Geran-3 attack drones struck an industrial facility in Zaporizhzhia, setting vehicles and a building ablaze; the strike followed an earlier afternoon drone attack on the city that injured 7 people and set roughly 10 vehicles on fire, according to regional administration head Ivan Fedorov. The same evening, a Geran-3 drone hit a residential area of Kharkiv's Osnovianskyi district, damaging 6 houses and 5 cars and injuring 4 people, 3 of whom suffered acute stress reactions, per Kharkiv Oblast Military Administration head Oleh Syniehubov.

title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Afipsky and Novoshakhtinsk Refineries, Kill 2 in Krasnodar
detail: Ukrainian long-range drones struck Russia's Afipsky oil refinery in Krasnodar Krai (about 375 km from the front line) overnight into August 25, sparking a major fire. Regional governor Veniamin Kondratyev said falling drone debris killed 2 people and injured 2 others near the Afipsky railway station, and that at least 10 private homes in the town of Afipsky were damaged, one of them catching fire. Ukrainian forces also struck the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery in Rostov Oblast and the Astrakhan gas processing plant the same night; the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez refinery in Perm Krai, hit on August 21, remained offline. Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service said the sustained refinery campaign has contributed to a 19% drop in Russian wheat export prices.

title: CIA Director Ratcliffe Makes Unannounced Moscow Visit; Ukraine Pauses Strikes on Moscow, St. Petersburg
detail: CIA Director John Ratcliffe made a rare, unannounced trip to Moscow on August 25, flying via U.S. Air Force aircraft from Riga to Vnukovo Airport and departing the same day — his first publicly known visit to Russia since becoming CIA director. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Ratcliffe did not meet President Putin, describing the contacts as occurring 'at the intelligence agencies' level,' and declined further detail. U.S. officials confirmed the trip but would not disclose its substance; analysts said Ukraine, Iran, and Russia's military posture were likely topics. A source told Kyiv Independent the U.S. had asked Ukraine to refrain from striking Moscow and St. Petersburg between August 24 and 26 during the visit, reportedly out of concern that a strike could embarrass Ratcliffe's hosts; Kyiv agreed to the temporary pause.
